questions.stem: For a reaction with $\Delta H < 0$ and $\Delta S < 0$, the reaction is spontaneous

options.whyWrong: High $T$ makes the positive $-T\Delta S$ term dominate, so $\Delta G > 0$.
True only if $\Delta S > 0$ as well.
At low enough $T$ the negative $\Delta H$ dominates, so $\Delta G < 0$.

questions.solution:
**Key idea:** $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$.

- $\Delta H < 0$ favours spontaneity.
- $\Delta S < 0$ makes $-T\Delta S > 0$, and this grows with $T$.
- So $\Delta G < 0$ only while $T < \Delta H / \Delta S$: **spontaneous at low temperatures**.
hints: Write $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$ and check the sign of each term.
